CREATION_RULE_CONTEXT.NETWORK_ENVIRONMENT_CONSTRAINTS: Deterministic offline/local benchmark runtime; no dependence on cloud credentials, privileged external infrastructure, internet services, or destructive host routing. Simulate or namespace route operations safely while preserving realistic Linux routing semantics and Ansible-managed multi-node behavior.

APPROVED_WORK_PACKAGE.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Build a production-style Go route control plane that models desired route and policy state, reconciles it across a multi-node Linux fleet, detects drift, protects management reachability, records revision history, and exposes the same lifecycle through an operator dashboard and Ansible-driven installation/configuration.
REQUIREMENT_FAMILIES: policy routing rules and named tables
fleet rollout waves and failure isolation
dashboard inventory, route, drift, rollout and revision views
PRESERVATION_OBLIGATIONS: never mutate the benchmark host routing table
rejected changes leave serving state unchanged
unchanged nodes remain stable across retries
management-safety routes cannot be removed without a safe replacement
revision and audit history remains monotonic
Ansible reruns do not duplicate service or config state

REQUIRED_END_STATE: At least 16 route-control API operations cover nodes, tables, routes, rules, revisions, previews, applies, rollbacks, drift, reconcile, rollouts, audit, health and dashboard summary.
All route mutations are performed against an isolated deterministic kernel model rather than the CI host network.
Desired and observed state are revisioned and recoverable after restart.
Per-node failures are isolated during wave rollout and support rollback.
Ansible installs the binary/config/service and projects host/group variables idempotently.
The frontend exposes network inventory, route/rule tables, revisions, drift and rollout controls.

STATE_MODEL.persistence: Atomic JSON checkpoint containing schema version, monotonic revision, nodes, desired revisions, observed snapshots, rollouts and audit sequence. Writes use temp-file + fsync-like atomic replace semantics in the model; startup validates and falls back to last-known-good backup on corrupt primary.
STATE_MODEL.concurrency: One store-level compare-and-swap revision plus per-node apply serialization; read snapshots are immutable copies.
STATE_MODEL.safety: Management CIDRs/interfaces and protected routes are explicit node policy. Plans that strand protected reachability are rejected before publication.

SOLVER_VISIBLE_DOC_PLAN: README.md for architecture and local run
docs/api.md for endpoints and request/response schemas
docs/routing-semantics.md for route/rule identity, multipath normalization and safety
docs/ansible.md for inventory variables and rollout
PRODUCTION_CHARACTERISTICS: layered Go packages with interfaces between orchestration and kernel model
operator dashboard consuming the same API
outputs.DATA_VOLUME_PLAN: Seed 8 deterministic nodes across three sites, 14 named route tables, IPv4/IPv6 routes, multipath entries, policy rules, drift fixtures and multiple historical revisions; expand through deterministic fixtures for test breadth without synthetic business-record padding.
